vertical_slice_diversity_notes: Primary source coverage is narrow: 2 gov/ministry sources cover only clinic counts (Indonesia and Malaysia). All cost anchors, time benchmarks, and frequency figures rely on academic preprints (arXiv), salary aggregators, or US/Singapore proxies. No top-tier consultancy authored report (McKinsey, BCG, Deloitte), no industry association report (MMA, IDI, PHEI), no audited corporate filing, and no direct interview transcript cited across the full stage. Geography mismatch is pervasive: 8 of 48 claims use non-ID/MY data as proxy. The claim category with the most evidential weight (pain point cost anchors) has the least primary sourcing.
gate_reasoning: Of 48 claims scored, only 2 are High confidence (VC-MS-1: Indonesia clinic count from Kemenkes; and implicitly the two Medium claims VC-S1a-7b and VC-S1a-8a that are the strongest in the document). 41 of 48 claims (85%) are Low confidence. The core cost anchors that drive the business case — documentation labor cost (PP1.1), ICD-10 error rate and associated claim rejection cost (PP1.2), front-desk verification delay cost (PP1.3), and history reconstruction cost (PP1.4) — are all Low, built from salary aggregators, US proxy data, Puskesmas PoC extrapolations, and assumed frequencies. Eight auto-Low vendor-marketing overrides are triggered. Twelve geography mismatches are flagged. Three stale-source overrides fire. The underlying structural narrative is coherent and the pain points are real, but the current evidence base cannot support a sourced business case. Six weak claims have been identified for targeted deep-research, prioritized in the following order: (1) ID/MY private GP documentation time share — the single most impactful upgrade, (2) FKTP-level ICD-10 coding error rate from BPJS administrative data, (3) national FKTP EMR adoption from Kemenkes SATUSEHAT data rather than a single vendor proxy, (4) Malaysian TPA claim rejection rate from Bank Negara Malaysia or MMA data, (5) GP salary from BPS/DOSM primary labor statistics, (6) Malaysia clinic count corroboration. A targeted deep-research pass addressing items 1-3 would materially upgrade the confidence distribution.
data_gaps_confirmed: National average daily patient volume per private GP clinic (ID and MY): no government or association statistic found
Malaysia private GP EHR adoption rate 2023: no MOH Malaysia or MMA statistic; HK 2015 proxy used
Indonesia FKTP EMR adoption: single-vendor data only; Kemenkes SATUSEHAT aggregate not yet published or found
Sub-step-level time benchmarks for ID/MY private clinics: all from public clinic or US data
BPJS PCare portal uptime statistics: not published by BPJS Kesehatan
FKTP-level ICD-10 coding error rate: all published studies from hospitals, not FKTP outpatient
Willingness-to-pay for any AI intervention in ID/MY GP clinic context: no published WTP study found
